TRANSPARENT BY DESIGN

Follow the flow.

A workflow you trigger. Calculations you can inspect.

The same Python behind every run

The interface reads Excel locally and sends normalized rows to a Python worker in your browser. The worker calls workflow.py and your bond_engine.py. Results return to the interface for review and Excel export.

The source package includes the application, Python engine, workflow documentation, tests, and GitHub Actions checks. The valuation itself runs when you click “Run valuation”; it does not send your portfolio to GitHub Actions.

Open GitHub repository →
NO BLACK BOX

Know what’s behind the number.

Explicit conventions. Inspectable Python. Your workbook stays on your device.

Cash flows & present value

Interest = notional × annual coupon rate × period year fraction. Principal is repaid once, at maturity. Dirty PV is the sum of discounted future payments; clean PV subtracts accrued interest.

DF = exp(−r × actual days / 365)

Discount rates are flat, continuously compounded annual zero rates. Choose rates that reflect your funding and credit assumptions. This tool does not fetch live market rates.

Floating rate bonds

The current period requires its known reference fixing, excluding spread. Future rates are simple forwards implied by the projection curve, plus spread.

Forward = (DF(start) / DF(end) − 1) / accrual

Floating forecasts change with rates. Overnight compounded SOFR/SONIA, reset lags, caps, floors, and embedded options are outside this version’s scope.

Dates & conventions

Schedules run backward from maturity, preserve month-end, and allow a short first stub. Supported day counts: ACT/360, ACT/365F and European 30E/360.

There are no business-day or holiday adjustments. Payments on settlement are excluded. This version supports bullet bonds, without amortization, ex-coupon rules, or optionality.

Workbooks & source code

Choose your worksheet and header row, then map columns. Required bond information must be present in the workbook or supplied as a fallback. Arbitrary spreadsheet layouts do not imply missing financial data.

Outputs include Valuations, Cash Flows, Inputs, Errors, and Run Info. Currency totals are never combined across currencies.
